results.fact: Header/area elevation vs. this route's actual summit
results.evidence: Already consistent: the route has since been re-filed on its own area wa_tepeh_towers, whose live elevation_ft is 8,113, matching high_point_ft 8,113 and the Summit waypoint 8,113. The header no longer shows Eldorado's 8,872.

New sources only add data points, not a window: one documented ascent was made on 16 May 2021 on crampons and snow (so snow climbing before June is possible), another car-to-car ascent on 6 Sep 2019. Neither says anything about October. The season chip (Jun-Sep) vs best_season/seasonal_guidance (Jul-Oct) remains unsettled by two agreeing sources.

Still split. For 5.6: the Mountaineers West Side route page, a 2005 and a 2015 trip report. For 5.3: Wikipedia and a 2001 report ('reported to be 5.3'). Two further first-hand ascents (2019, 2021) grade it only as 'low 5th class' / 'fifth class' with delicate moves past one rusty bolt, which does not pick a side. Nothing supports 5.4. Adopting a grade would require rewriting ~10 fields (grade, overview, beta, hazards, descent_text, pro_tips, climbing_route, itinerary) and is left for a decision.

New first-hand accounts disagree with each other: a 2021 party made two rappels on two 30 m ropes, the first 'just barely' reaching; a 2019 party made three rappels on a single 60 m rope (past the crux, below loose blocks, past slabs). A Mountaineers report describes one double-rope rap. No count or rope length is confirmed by two sources; the rappels prose's claim that a single 60 m reaches from the summit in one rap is supported by none of them.

Round trips from two more first-hand reports: 16 mi (2021) and 16.5 mi (2019), close to the row's 16-16.5 mi. But the disputed fields are the waypoint distMi values (Prusik Pass 9.5, base 10) and the 3-day 19-20 mi total, and no source states a one-way mileage to the base or a 3-day total; deriving one by halving is not allowed.

Figures still disagree: 8,000 ft (2021 report, matching gain_ft), ~7,300 and ~7,400 ft (earlier reports), and 6,972 ft stated as the trailhead-to-summit range in the 2019 report (matching loss_ft ~6,995 but that is a net figure). No two sources agree on a car-to-car total.

No new source states a cumulative gain for the East Peak. Search results only restate the 3,600-7,520 ft range (net 3,920). The cascadeclimbers reports (2004, 2022) and the nwhikers thread would not load; peakery has no route stats.

results.fact: Number and length of the summit rappel
results.evidence: A search summary of a 2004 report says that party made a double 30 m rope rappel back along the east ridge, but that report went to the Middle (main) summit, not the East Peak, and its page could not be loaded to confirm. Still only one East Peak account (two 30 m raps with rope plus tagline).

results.fact: gain_ft/loss_ft (5,600) vs itinerary gain total and totalNote (5,400)
results.evidence: All other published figures (4,000+, 4,200, 4,400 ft over ~15-16 mi) are for the South Peak lookout trail, which does not include the ~400 ft drop to the glacier and ~1,000 ft regain to the Middle/North col. No second source for the North Peak total was found.

results.fact: dist_km (Approach one way) 22.53 km = 14.0 mi vs Summit waypoint 7.3 mi and itinerary 14.5 mi round trip
results.evidence: dist_km renders as 'Approach (one way)' but holds ~14 mi, roughly the round trip (itinerary 4.5+5.5+4.5 = 14.5 mi; the summit pin sits at 7.3 mi). No source states a one-way distance to North Peak (published figures are 15-16 mi round trip to the South Peak lookout), and halving a round trip is not allowed, so no patch.

results.fact: One-way approach distance (dist_km 8.85 km = 5.5 mi) vs summit waypoint distMi 5.0 and itinerary 10 mi RT
results.evidence: Only round trips exist: 7.7 mi RT (2360-6687 ft) for the main peak by the southeast shoulder, and 10 mi / 4,600 ft for Middle Peak by the south face. Neither states a one-way distance and they disagree with each other; SummitPost and WTA pages returned 403. No patch.
